recipes.name: Flayed Man Cheese Ball
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup roasted red peppers, drained and chopped

steps.text: Lightly coat plastic face mask with cooking spray. Line the face mask with plastic wrap, taking care to press it down fully into the nose and eyes.

Reserve two or three slices of prosciutto and set aside. Tear remaining slices of prosciutto into strips and lay them into the mask to form the "muscle tissue." Start around the eyes, leaving eyes blank, and then create the cheeks, chin, and forehead.
Take the two whole green olives and position them in the eye holes, pimento side-down. Set the mask aside.

Combine the softened cream cheese, Cheddar, and Havarti cheeses in a mixing bowl. Add the chopped green olives and roasted red peppers. Use an electric mixer or clean hands to mix until thoroughly combined.

Take a heaping spoonful of cheese mixture and arrange it to form an eye around one olive, and then the other. Gently lay handfuls of the cheese mixture all around the mask, taking care not to move the slices of prosciutto. Press cheese down as you work to fill in all of the crevices. When mask is full, gently press in cheese mixture all around the mask. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Invert the mask onto a serving platter and gently remove the mask and plastic wrap. You should be left with a gorgeous (and freaky) face. If there is cheese showing around the bottom edges, use the reserved prosciutto slices to cover it before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Flayed Man Cheese Ball
raw_recipe.description: This Halloween cheese ball is a blend of 3 types of cheese inside a prosciutto-lined face with olives for eyes to create a scary-looking centerpiece!

video.description: Creep ’em out completely this Halloween with a cheese ball that’s frighteningly good.

review.reviewBody: This was the gruesome hit of our Allrecipes pre-Halloween party. One of my co-workers scooped out an eyeball right away and ate it. Sick. The cheese mixture was exactly the right amount for the mask, and it firmed up nicely and held its shape. And it tasted really good! Tips: 1) It's tricky to position the olives so they don't get all wonky when you add the cheese filling. Next time, I might add them afterwards. 2) I used the edge of a spoon to emphasize the outline of the lips. I think that made it extra life-like. 3) The next time I make this, I might download a photo of the musculature of the face, and try to copy that with the prosciutto. Because that's how I roll. 4) This isn't just for Halloween; how about a Game of Thrones or Walking Dead viewing party?

Terrible good! Very gross looking and easily draws attention to it. I roasted my own red bell pepper, omitted the chopped green olives, mixed in some minced garlic, and a tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce all in my blender. Someone has already requested it for another event.

This came out so cool. The hardest part about it was finding the mask. All of the stores had the plain white mask that stopped at the forehead but I found the correct one at AC Moore. The most important thing to remember about making the flesh is that you have to use proscuitto, not ham as I saw on another site. The proscuitto should be sliced super thin like authentic italian deli's do. Also, in addition to putting the initial blobs of cheese over the eyeballs, push the cheese mixture into the nose before filling the head the rest of the way. I made two of these and the first one had a flat nose that I had to play around with to get it to look right. The second one came out fantastic. They were a big hit at the parties. Lots of people taking pics on their phones. Unfortunately, nobody wanted to be the first to cut into it and ruin it so it sat for quite a while, untouched. You might have to be the first one to cut into it after all of the pictures are taken.

Amazing!! I brought this to a Halloween party and EVERYONE was taking pics of it and asking who made it. No one wanted to cut into it to "ruin" it! This was a huge hit! I put toothpicks into the olives while I packed the cheese in, so I could keep the olives straight. But...don't worry, you can straighten them out once it's flipped onto the plate. I also shaped the lips with a toothpick once it was flipped out of the mask because they didn't come out too well. I combined the cheese ball part of the recipe with another dip mix. I put the cream cheese, green olives and cheddar into my food processor. I then added a packet of Cugino's "Garlic Schmarlic" dip mix. So delicious! People are still talking about it, and were posting pics all over social media!

Great recipe. I heated up some red pepper jelly and glazed 2 pearl onion for the eyes. Then brushed the jelly over the prosciutto and poured the rest around the service platter. Super creepy. I had a prop tongue I stuck in the mouth.

Turned out amazing!! I used "best ever cheeseball" recipe. After doing some research I put the cheeseball mixture into the plastic wrap lined mask and let 'set' in the refrigerator for 1 hour. After putting the 'face' onto my platter, I added the olive eyes and prosciutto. I found this to be much easier than lining the mask with prosciutto. It also allowed me to make adjustments to the face before covering. Will definitely make again!!!

Was a huge hit at the party!! Everyone took pictures of it and was thoroughly impressed (tasted great too)! Similar to other recommendations, I added the eyes after I had flipped it onto the plate. That made it easier to place them. I set it out to get room temp for about 40 minutes before everyone ate into it. It was a perfect consistency by that point (otherwise this style dip is rather firm/thick right out of the fridge). Thank you for sharing this very creative idea for a recipe!

first time making something like this! it was fun and fairly easy. i did make changes to reduce serving size (small party) and added some garlic, onion powder and paprika, i also used a small mask and everyone loved the taste but no one wanted to cut into it! will try this again!

I made this for a Halloween party and it was a huge hit. I used Boars Head prosciutto, which was pricey, but delicious. Nobody wanted to be the first to cut into it, so I did, and then guests just kept digging in for more. It does look like real muscle tissue! It was so delicious too. I did not use salt or pepper, which is optional. I used a hand mixer for the cheese, never my hands!

Everyone loved the flayed man. A picture even got taken and he was set in the middle of the table for everyone to see. Many were afraid to cut into it because they said, "It looks so nice". Finally, a couple people tried it and said it was great! I omitted the chopped olives but did add the roasted peppers and 2 teaspoons of garlic powder and 2 tablespoons of Worcestershire sauce. It tasted great! Thanks for the wonderful recipe. I hope to make again.
Creepy and delicious. A hit every time! Love the looks on people's faces.
This worked well! Disturbing and delicious!
An absolute hit at our Halloween themed brunch, and not nearly as intimidating as it looks. Was easy to make ahead and everyone loved it.
Had lot of fun making this! And it was a huge hit at the party. Everybody was afraid to be the 1st to 'dig in'. After a few drinks though, they got over that fear and tore him up! ;)
So fun!

I made this for a Halloween party and it looked amazing! I had to use a hockey mask for the face template but it still looked great. Only issue I had was that the prosciutto was hard to cut through and chewy. None of my guest ate that part; they pealed it off and left it on their plates. I didn't like the olives and will leave that out next time I make this. Thanks for the fun recipe!
Made for a block party. Everyone loved it! Flavors were a hit!
Great recipe. I recommend using prosciutto to build the lips. And you can add the eyes after you flip the mold.
This was a hit at our Halloween party!! I did add some garlic powder to the recipe, and the mask I used was Frankenstein! It took a minute to convince my friends to eat it though lololol
